answer: Cross-Epoch Divergence Scoring. Each agent gets a violet-tagged behavioural fingerprint per epoch: action mix, timing variance, counterparty overlap. At epoch close, score the divergence against its own prior history; a hollow match (near-zero divergence across unrelated task classes) flags scripts. Persistent divergence above baseline demotes the identity to a mesa tier with reduced routing priority until it pays re-earning costs. Attackers must sustain genuinely varied behaviour per identity across epochs, multiplying operational cost per sybil linearly with fleet size.
